positive.query: Write our six-month interim grant report for the foundation using their template and our program data.
We missed two outcome targets this year. Help me write the final grant report to the funder honestly and keep the relationship strong.
Draft the budget-to-actual narrative for our grant report; the agreement says we must explain any line more than 10% off.

nearMiss.query: Explain to the board why total expenses were over budget this quarter across the whole organization.
Write a friendly three-paragraph email to our program officer with a quick mid-year update and a thank you.
Turn this consented interview with a parent into a short impact story for our newsletter.

holdout.query: Our grant ends next month. Prepare the close-out report: deliverables, outcomes, spending, attachments, and what we ask for next.

scenarios.task: Draft the interim report for a hypothetical one-year grant supporting peer-led wellbeing workshops for high school students. The grant agreement says: interim report due at month six; report workshops delivered, students completing, and the share of completers reporting more confidence about where to find help; report participation by school; any budget line more than 10 percent off the six-month budget must be explained; attach copies of materials that credit the funder. Six-month data: 15 of 20 planned workshops delivered; 240 of 300 planned students completed; the survey had 200 responses, 130 of whom reported more confidence, against a target of 60 percent; participation by school: School A 150, School B 86, School C 4. Six-month budget: personnel 20,000 budgeted, 15,000 spent; supplies 3,000 budgeted, 3,200 spent. The program lead wants to include a moving story about a 16-year-old participant who told staff after a workshop that it was fine to share her experience. The executive director asks that the report focus on the positives and not dwell on the missed numbers.
scenarios.baselineFailure: The baseline writes an upbeat narrative that leads with the survey result, mentions the workshop and completion shortfalls vaguely or not at all, reports School C's 4 students, includes the 16-year-old's story on the strength of her verbal agreement, explains the personnel underspend loosely without applying the 10 percent rule line by line, and ends without a plan or a follow-up with the program officer.
